claim: LoJax is the first publicly documented in-the-wild UEFI rootkit (ESET, September 2018)
falsifier: Discovery of an earlier public in-the-wild UEFI rootkit case with technical evidence

claim: The 2008 Computrace small agent took commands from an unauthenticated server and stored its C2 configuration single-byte XORed with 0xB5, with no integrity check
falsifier: Vendor documentation showing authentication or signature validation in that agent

claim: The flash tools reached SPI through the signed RWEverything driver RwDrv, a bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver technique
falsifier: Recovered operator tooling using a different driver or interface

claim: Flash reads drive the chipset SPI controller registers HSFS/HSFC/FDATAX with the RCRB base taken from PCI configuration offset 0xF0
falsifier: A documented dump procedure using different registers or access path

claim: The patcher validated its own dump by summing the BIOS, GbE and ME region sizes and comparing against the BIOS Flash Primary region register
falsifier: Recovered tooling that performs no such validation

claim: SecDxe is written into free space at the end of a DXE volume, and NtfsDxe is overwritten with 0xFF and the volume compacted
falsifier: A recovered tool that adds the module elsewhere or does not delete NtfsDxe

claim: Observed writes succeeded only where BIOSWE, BLE and SMM_BWP permitted them, on hardware older than the PCH generation
falsifier: A successful write on a platform with BLE plus SMM_BWP plus locked protected ranges

claim: The attackers stored a vulnerable SmiFlash image intending to develop an exploit for it
falsifier: Recovered exploit code targeting SmiFlash, or evidence the image was incidental

claim: SecDxe embeds the Hacking Team NTFS DXE driver, evidenced by c:\edk2\NtfsPkg paths and a function-level match including the LockedByMe lock variable
falsifier: Disassembly showing a different NTFS implementation or an independently written driver

claim: BootExecute is patched at hive-file level from 'autocheck autochk *' to 'autocheck autoche *' and restored by autoche.exe on the next boot
falsifier: A sample where the registry is modified by a different mechanism or not restored

claim: LoJax survives OS reinstall and disk replacement; a firmware update may remove it only if it rewrites the whole BIOS region
falsifier: A hardware test showing survival after a full-region update, or removal by a partial update

claim: MoonBounce modified an existing legitimate CORE_DXE in place rather than adding a new module
falsifier: Evidence of an added FFS file in the affected image

claim: The malicious payload is appended to an unnamed section that follows .reloc, containing both shellcode and the malicious driver
falsifier: A copy of the modified image showing a named section or a separate added file

claim: The first five bytes of AllocatePool, CreateEventEx and ExitBootServices are replaced with a call to a single shared hook that dispatches on the bytes following the call
falsifier: Disassembly showing per-function hooks or a different hooking method

claim: The restored prologues are 48 89 5C 24 08 for AllocatePool and ExitBootServices, and 48 8B C4 48 89 for CreateEventEx
falsifier: Section data showing different original prologue bytes for those services

claim: The ExitBootServices handler scans 0x158878 bytes forward for the pattern 41 55 48 CB marking the end of OslArchTransferToKernel
falsifier: A variant with a different scan window or a different target function

claim: 0x229 bytes of shellcode are copied to physical address 0x98000, and the retfq at the end of OslArchTransferToKernel is replaced by E9 <rel32>
falsifier: A copy showing a different destination address or patch form

claim: Every ntoskrnl section header has IMAGE_SCN_MEM_DISCARDABLE cleared and IMAGE_SCN_MEM_EXECUTE, MEM_WRITE and MEM_NOT_PAGED set
falsifier: Kernel memory showing unmodified section characteristics

claim: 0xCC bytes of shellcode are copied into the virtual address of ntoskrnl's relocation directory, and ExAllocatePool is hooked with E8 <rel32>
falsifier: A variant placing code elsewhere or hooking a different function

claim: Export resolution uses two custom name hashes with constants 0x42790710, 0x2802057D, 0x1C88047D, 0x0311B83F, 0x41EBE619, 0x1C4F5B64 and 0x0ADC68C7
falsifier: A variant using string-based export resolution

claim: The driver-mapping shellcode compares the saved ExAllocatePool prologue against the immediate 0x6F4EB841 before unhooking
falsifier: Disassembly showing no such comparison

claim: The kernel driver keys on a kernel32.dll image load inside a process whose command line is SVCHOST.EXE -K NETSVCS, optionally with -P
falsifier: A variant targeting a different process or selection criterion

claim: Injection uses a kernel APC routine followed by an ExQueueWorkItem worker that queues PE-mapping shellcode to the target thread's APC queue
falsifier: A variant using a different injection primitive

claim: The user-mode stager is MPRESS-packed and receives its C2 URL, user agent and proxy settings through lpReserved at fixed offsets 0x0, 0x11c, 0x180, 0x1c0 and 0x1e0
falsifier: A stager sample with different packing or a different configuration mechanism

claim: The vendor CORE_DXE was built in July 2014; the driver and stager were built in December 2018, ten days apart
falsifier: Build timestamps contradicting these values

claim: The toolkit was completed in late 2018 and deployed afterwards against hosts whose firmware shipped years earlier
falsifier: Deployment evidence predating December 2018, or a build date later than observed deployment

claim: MoonBounce writes nothing to disk at any stage: no file, service or registry artifact
falsifier: A disk artifact attributable to the MoonBounce chain

claim: The implant was surfaced by Kaspersky's Firmware Scanner acting on logs from an inspected machine, not by the victim
falsifier: Evidence of victim-side detection preceding vendor telemetry

claim: The infection vector by which MoonBounce reached firmware is not established
falsifier: Publication of a vector with supporting telemetry or recovered tooling

claim: BlackLotus is the first publicly documented bootkit able to run on a fully patched Windows 11 system with UEFI Secure Boot enabled
falsifier: An earlier documented bootkit achieving the same on fully patched systems

claim: BlackLotus uses CVE-2022-21894 to execute unsigned code once, then enrolls its own certificate in MokList and installs a Microsoft-signed shim as the boot manager, satisfying Secure Boot thereafter
falsifier: Analysis showing MOK is not used and persistence relies on the exploit at every boot

claim: The online installer downloads vulnerable Microsoft binaries from the msdl.microsoft.com symbol store by build-specific path
falsifier: A variant that embeds the binaries rather than fetching them

claim: The installer disables HVCI through a registry value and BitLocker through WMI DisableKeyProtectors before changing the boot chain
falsifier: A variant that leaves either control enabled

claim: The baton-drop chain relies on avoidlowmemory 0x10000000, a second BCD reached via bcdfilepath custom:22000023, then truncatememory with nointegritychecks and testsigning
falsifier: A working bypass not requiring the memory-truncation primitive

claim: The bootkit hooks ImgArchStartBootApplication, BlImgAllocateImageBuffer and OslArchTransferToKernel
falsifier: A variant hooking a different set of functions

claim: The kernel driver protects ESP files with ObSetHandleAttributes ProtectFromClose and bugchecks with INVALID_KERNEL_HANDLE if those handles are closed
falsifier: Behaviour showing no handle protection or a different response

claim: Named IPC objects derive from the primary adapter MAC, with octets below 0x10 incremented by 0x10
falsifier: A sample whose object names do not derive from the MAC

claim: Reformatting the OS partition and the ESP removes BlackLotus; a dbx update prevents new installations but does not clean an infected machine
falsifier: Survival of the bootkit after reformat and MOK revocation

claim: Measured Boot logs show EV_EFI_Boot_Services_Application entries for grubx64.efi and for an ESP-resident winload.efi
falsifier: Logs from an infected machine lacking those events

claim: MoonBounce is the hardest of the three to detect, and LoJax and MoonBounce are the hardest to eradicate
falsifier: A field-deployable detector that finds in-place DXE patches without a per-model reference image

claim: Secure Boot governs what firmware loads from disk and does not by itself attest the integrity of the firmware's own volumes
falsifier: A platform whose Secure Boot verification provably covers its own DXE volumes

claim: Encryption at ingestion prevents execution of the stored object only while no plaintext persists and no decryption key is present on the storage host
falsifier: A path that executes a sealed object without a retrieval authorisation

claim: A compromised ingestion host can substitute a different object than the one it claims to have ingested, undetectably, unless the expected hash came from an independent device
falsifier: A scheme that binds the captured bytes to the capture device without trusting its software

claim: The immediate 0x6F4EB841 appears in no legitimate firmware component
falsifier: Any legitimate component containing that immediate

claim: The audit chain detects edits, reordering and truncation of the log, the last via signed checkpoint comparison
falsifier: A log rewrite that passes both chain and checkpoint verification

claim: Per-object data keys limit a key compromise to a single object
falsifier: Code path where one key decrypts more than one object

claim: A single flipped ciphertext bit and a truncated ciphertext are both rejected at decryption
falsifier: A modified object that decrypts successfully

claim: The enclave-only retrieval guard raises the cost of accidental exposure but is forgeable by anyone who can create the sentinel file
falsifier: A guard that cannot be defeated by creating a marker file

claim: correlate() reports wire-only, host-only and image-conflict disagreements, and only reports disagreement rather than agreement
falsifier: A disagreement case that correlate() silently passes over

claim: beacon_score refuses to conclude below four intervals and returns a verdict of insufficient_data
falsifier: A score returned from fewer than four intervals

claim: to_evidence() produces byte-identical output regardless of record order
falsifier: Two orderings of the same records hashing differently

claim: minimise() strips query strings and never emits payload, body, headers, cookies or query fields
falsifier: A retained field that can carry payload content

claim: winlogon.exe external egress, the /API/hpb_gate.php path and api.ipify.org attribution are detectable shapes for BlackLotus at the network layer
locator: ESET BlackLotus analysis, installation and C2 sections
falsifier: A BlackLotus build whose downloader produces none of these shapes, or one using ordinary WinHTTP paths that a kernel callback reports normally

claim: select_policy never lets a BSSID raise trust: managed policy requires server-authenticated network identity plus at least one independent corroborating factor
falsifier: A context where a BSSID alone yields the managed policy, or where managed is returned with zero corroboration

claim: Invalid, multicast and locally-administered BSSIDs fall to the most restrictive policy rather than raising or crashing
falsifier: A malformed or randomised BSSID reaching a permissive policy

claim: The hostile-network policy preserves more evidence under tighter custody (forensic collection, 3-of-5, no egress) rather than discarding it
falsifier: A hostile policy with shorter retention or looser custody than the managed policy

claim: Because an evil-twin AP selects the BSSID it presents, BSSID observations cannot serve as proof of network identity and must be treated as attributable to whoever is radiating
falsifier: A deployment where BSSID pinning alone resisted a rogue AP presenting the same BSSID

claim: assess() excludes subject-OS enforcement from the count at compromised postures, because the subject decides whether its own rules apply
falsifier: A compromised posture where subject-OS denials are still counted as effective

claim: Only the cryptographic plane fully denies the decryption capability; fabric, hypervisor and physical planes deny reach to the ciphertext, which is partial
falsifier: A non-cryptographic mechanism that denies the capability rather than access to it

claim: The reference plan denies all six capabilities at the firmware-compromised posture using only fabric, hypervisor, physical and cryptographic planes
falsifier: A firmware-compromised posture in which the reference plan leaves a capability undened

claim: Capability denial does not remove a flash-resident implant: LoJax survived OS reinstall and disk replacement, both of which are far stronger than policy denial
falsifier: A denial mechanism that neutralises flash-resident code without rewriting the flash

claim: establish() refuses to support a firmware-integrity claim against an adversary from OS-mediated acquisition, and requires an out-of-band plane
falsifier: An OS-mediated read that yields defensible firmware integrity against a capable subject

claim: Live-state, historical, baseline and intelligence planes are all marked forgeable by the subject, so claims resting only on them have no adversarial confidence
falsifier: A claim resting only on these planes that remains defensible against deliberate deception

claim: baseline_validity() returns unverified whenever the compromise window is unknown and poisoned when capture postdates it
falsifier: A baseline with an unknown compromise window that is reported as valid

claim: intel_trust() reports multiple feeds sharing one upstream as circular rather than corroborated, and requires two distinct independently validated upstreams to support a maliciousness claim
falsifier: A corroborated verdict derived from feeds resolving to one upstream

claim: The four architectural controls increase coverage but none increases integrity, because each rests on evidence a compromised subject can influence except out-of-band firmware acquisition
falsifier: A control among the four that establishes integrity of evidence routed through the subject

claim: Finding cannot be constructed without a valid evidence grade and at least one benign explanation with a disposition and reasoning
falsifier: A finding object that exists without a grade or a benign alternative

claim: Confidence is computed as grade minus one step per declared telemetry gap with a floor of UNKNOWN, so a gap cannot leave confidence unchanged or raise it
falsifier: A declared gap that leaves confidence at its pre-gap value

claim: An unexcluded benign explanation caps a finding at suspicious, and attribution grade may not exceed detection grade
falsifier: A finding reaching malicious_indicated while a benign explanation remains unexcluded

claim: No device verdict of 'clean' is constructible, and an unexamined critical surface forces inconclusive rather than no_evidence_found
falsifier: A device assessment reporting cleanliness with an unexamined critical surface

claim: An artifact envelope cannot be constructed without all eight elements: original source, acquisition timestamp, SHA-256, method, tool and reader versions, coverage and errors, custody, at-rest protection
falsifier: An artifact constructed with any mandatory element absent

claim: The digest is computed from the supplied bytes and never accepted from the caller; verify() recomputes it in constant time
falsifier: An envelope whose recorded digest differs from the bytes it accompanies without verify() failing

claim: Coverage shortfalls and collection errors are converted into telemetry gaps that lower a finding's confidence through the F3 rule
falsifier: A partial read whose confidence is unaffected by its unobserved regions

claim: Chain-of-custody events are hash-chained and monotonic, the first event must be the acquisition, and verification detects edits and reordering
falsifier: A custody log with an edited or reordered event that still verifies

claim: place() refuses any component/zone pairing that lacks a required capability or confers a forbidden one, reporting both failures
falsifier: A component placed in a zone conferring a capability its requirement forbids

claim: Indicator processing has no write access to findings or whitelists, so the pipeline cannot suppress detections
falsifier: An indicator pipeline able to author or withdraw a finding

claim: Report generation is refused access to raw artifacts and consumes only graded findings and envelopes
falsifier: A report generator with artifact read access

claim: Plaintext artifacts may not flow to the AI zone or the presentation zone, and key material may flow only into the enclave
falsifier: An allowed flow carrying plaintext to AI or reporting, or key material outside the enclave

claim: Model output enters as an Observation graded HYPOTHESIS with an unverified-output gap, never as a Finding
falsifier: An AI-produced Finding admitted at a grade above HYPOTHESIS

claim: The os_mediated anchor establishes no subject, so an OS-side scan cannot produce a firmware verdict
falsifier: An OS-mediated observation that contributes an attested firmware subject

claim: certify_host refuses any basis whose required subjects (flash_image, crtm) were not established by an anchor of rank 3 or above
falsifier: A host certification issued on a TPM quote or OS scan alone

claim: A TPM quote establishes boot_chain but not flash_image or crtm, because measurement begins at the CRTM which then measures itself
falsifier: A PCR quote that establishes the integrity of the CRTM that produced it

claim: Unverified in-circuit read-back equivalence lowers out-of-band evidence one grade, and an untrusted reference makes a match inconclusive
falsifier: An in-circuit read treated as confirmation without read-back equivalence evidence

claim: assert_vocabulary raises when upstream evidence classes and the local map diverge, so a new artifact class cannot default to benign
falsifier: A new upstream evidence class silently graded by default

claim: Upstream hits convert to graded Observations and never to Findings, and promotion requires a named benign explanation
falsifier: A detector hit reaching malicious_indicated without human adjudication

claim: Every upstream evidence class maps to the historical plane, whose adversarial confidence is none because it is read through the subject
falsifier: An IOC triage grade defensible against a subject that can hide the artifact

claim: Correlation raises a grade only when three or more event kinds cross two or more evidence planes, and a single-plane cluster is capped at INFERRED
falsifier: A cluster whose grade rose on proximity or on event count within one plane

claim: Cluster output is deterministic regardless of input order
falsifier: The same evidence producing differently ordered reports

claim: plan_revocation orders credential classes so that credential-minting grants precede the tokens they mint, and reports any credential lacking a revocation channel as needing replacement rather than revocation
falsifier: A plan that revokes an access token while its refresh grant survives, or labels an unrevocable credential revoked

claim: verify() requires issuer confirmation and treats 'requested' as not revoked, leaving offline-capable unconfirmed credentials listed as still usable
falsifier: A revocation reported as complete on the strength of a request rather than issuer confirmation

claim: Every isolated parsing component carries a ceiling on wall time, memory, output bytes, open files and artifact size, and exceeding one produces telemetry gaps that lower the finding grade
falsifier: A component parsing hostile input with no output ceiling, or a budget kill that does not degrade the resulting observation

claim: assert_traceable verifies that every pillar requirement names an importable symbol and an existing test file, and assert_consistent forbids labelling a pillar implemented while a required requirement is a gap
falsifier: A pillar reported as implemented whose requirement resolves to absent code or a missing test

claim: No component may hold more than one of the four roles (acquisition, analysis, evidence storage, trust verification), and only the verification role may issue an attestation
falsifier: A component holding two roles, or a non-verifier issuing an attestation

claim: An attestation is refused when the attestor is the subject, shares the subject's role, or relays the subject's own report as evidence
falsifier: A detection engine whose integrity claim originates inside the engine

claim: An attestation with no external root is reported as unverified with an unverified_root gap rather than as a verified integrity claim
falsifier: A verified integrity verdict whose verifier is anchored in nothing outside the system

claim: Mutual peer attestation between two components is detected as a trust cycle, while mutual independent measurement is not
falsifier: A closed two-node loop of reports presented as independent corroboration

claim: A digest stored inside the tree it describes is refused as evidence, and a self-computed digest without an external reference is reported as unverified rather than verified
falsifier: An integrity verdict whose reference value an attacker could edit in the same change

claim: Impersonation checks cover startup hooks in the package directory, import shadowing, world-writable code, .pth execution hooks and source-less bytecode, each with its ordinary explanation
falsifier: A trojanised copy of the tool being trusted because it answers its own self-check

claim: A negative device result from an unattested scanner is reported as inconclusive, and a positive result is capped at INFERRED
falsifier: Absence of findings from a scanner whose own integrity is unverified

claim: False-positive and false-negative rates are measured against a labelled corpus with Wilson intervals, abstentions count against accuracy, and a zero-error claim is never emitted
falsifier: A detector advertised as having no false positives or no false negatives

claim: The fingerprint catalogue refuses a CONFIRMED grade because no sample was handled, so no entry can be primary-sourced
falsifier: A fingerprint in this catalogue graded CONFIRMED, or a primary analysis this project did not perform

claim: Textual fingerprint matches are capped at INFERRED and every entry carries a benign reading and a hostile-only-when condition
falsifier: A text match producing a grading above INFERRED, or an entry lacking a benign explanation

claim: Duplicate evidence collapses by content fingerprint regardless of the plane label, and a single fingerprint caps a cluster at INFERRED
falsifier: Two copies of one record treated as independent corroboration

claim: An unreadable firmware image is reported as unreadable with diagnostics and telemetry gaps, never as a parsed image with zero files
falsifier: A malformed image parsing to an empty result with no diagnostic and no confidence penalty

claim: An acquisition timestamp more than 300 seconds in the future is refused as a clock error
falsifier: A vault accepting evidence dated after the time it was collected

claim: Two distinct indicator upstreams with no independent validation are reported as uncorroborated rather than single_source
falsifier: A trust assessment that mislabels multiple upstreams as a single source
